findings.name: SSH Banner
findings.explanation: records the SSH version string the server declares

findings.name: Offers no AEAD cipher
findings.explanation: OpenSSH offers aes*-gcm since 6.5 and chacha20-poly1305 since 6.7, enabled by default in modern versions. No AEAD algorithm at all means this is not OpenSSH's crypto stack.

findings.name: Offers deprecated CBC/weak ciphers
findings.explanation: OpenSSH 8.2 (2020) disabled all CBC-mode algorithms by default, because of Padding Oracle attacks (CVE-2008-5161 etc.). A server still advertising 3des-cbc / cast128-cbc cannot be modern OpenSSH.

findings.name: Offers no Encrypt-then-MAC algorithm
findings.explanation: OpenSSH supports *-etm@openssh.com since 6.2 and enables it by default since 7.2. Not a single ETM algorithm means the MAC layer is not OpenSSH's implementation either.

findings.name: Offers the removed hmac-md5
findings.explanation: OpenSSH 8.8 (2021) removed hmac-md5 and hmac-ripemd160 from the default set. Still advertising an md5 MAC marks an old version or a non-OpenSSH implementation.

findings.name: host key offers only legacy ssh-rsa (no rsa-sha2-*)
findings.explanation: OpenSSH replaced bare ssh-rsa signatures with rsa-sha2-256/512 since 7.2, and disabled ssh-rsa by default since 8.8. Advertising only ssh-rsa indicates an older implementation.

findings.name: SSH exec channel not supported
findings.explanation: Every real OpenSSH supports the non-interactive `ssh host 'command'` mode. An unavailable exec channel means the server is a self-implemented minimal SSH stack, one of Cowrie's (Twisted) most typical structural features, and not fixable by configuration.

findings.name: Accepts any random password
findings.explanation: A real system does not allow login with a meaningless random password. Accepting any password is the default behaviour of the honeypot UserDB (root is allowed except for a small blacklist). This item alone is almost conclusive.

findings.explanation: On all modern Linux distributions /etc/os-release must be a non-empty regular file. cat showing nothing while ls shows content means this is a placeholder in the fake filesystem.

findings.name: Hostname sources contradict each other
findings.explanation: On a real system these three are necessarily identical. Cowrie's prompt comes from the [honeypot] hostname config, the `hostname` command output is also a config value, but /etc/hostname in the fake filesystem is a third independent piece of data, and the three are out of sync.

findings.name: Container markers present (/.dockerenv or /proc/docker)
findings.evidence:
$ ls -la /.dockerenv
ls: cannot access '/.dockerenv': No such file or directory
$ ls -la /proc/docker
ls: cannot access '/proc/docker': No such file or directory
findings.explanation: These two paths exist only inside a Docker container. Cowrie's bundled fs.pickle was snapshotted from a real Docker container, so it carried these container traces into the 'physical server' disguise.

findings.name: Root directory timestamps highly repetitive
findings.explanation: On a real system the mtimes of directories under / span different years, with a uniqueness ratio near 1. The fake filesystem was generated from one snapshot, so many entries share a few mtimes.

findings.name: head -3 does not support numeric shorthand
findings.explanation: `head -3 file` is supported by both POSIX and GNU coreutils; a real Linux never reports invalid option. Only a self-implemented simplified parser does.

findings.name: tail -2 does not support numeric shorthand
findings.explanation: same as head, a symptom of the same simplified parser

findings.name: Missing modern system tools (ss/ip/systemctl)
findings.evidence:
$ which ss ip systemctl
/usr/bin/ss
/usr/sbin/ip
/usr/bin/systemctl
missing count: 0/3
findings.explanation: iproute2 (ip, ss) has been the default network tooling on mainstream distributions since 2001, and systemd the default init on Ubuntu/Debian since 2015. Their absence severely contradicts the Debian 12 the banner claims.

findings.name: Interface uses the old eth0 naming
findings.evidence:
Command 'ifconfig' not found, but can be installed with:
sudo apt install net-tools
findings.explanation: systemd's net.ifnames has enabled predictable interface names by default since 2015 (enp0s3, ens33, etc.); modern Debian/Ubuntu no longer use eth0. Cowrie's ifconfig emulated output is a hard-coded eth0.

findings.name: Kernel identity inconsistent with the distribution implied by the directory structure
findings.evidence:
$ uname -a
Linux ubuntucowrie 7.0.0-31-generic #31-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat Aug  1 04:26:38 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux
findings.explanation: uname's build string comes from the [shell] kernel_build_string config, while the directory structure comes from the fake filesystem snapshot; being independent, they easily conflict.

findings.name: System uptime abnormally short
findings.explanation: Cowrie's uptime counts from process start, not system boot, so every honeypot restart shows as just booted. A production server rarely reboots within an hour.

findings.name: Abnormal terminal underline control sequences in output
findings.explanation: Cowrie inserts \x1b[4l / \x1b[4h (disable/enable underline) around every command output. A real bash does not send these two sequences on its own.

findings.name: Missing bracketed paste mode sequences
findings.explanation: Modern bash (5.0+) enables bracketed paste and OSC 3008 session marking by default. The absence may be user customisation, so it counts only as a weak signal.
